chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Six or seven years in California with Eddie Heywood
summary: He went west with Heywood in the early 1940s, returned for the Three Deuces and Cafe Society, then got very sick and only came East in 1948 to play with Edmond Hall.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Was it '47 he died, huh?! Well, that's right. In '47... Oh, in the Forties I was out West. That's why I didn't run into anybody. I was out on the West Coast with Eddie Heywood.
And I think... Now that you mention it, I think he may have been out on the road for a few months or something, when he wasn't feeling well, and then he came back, and then...you know...
Yeah. But I was out on the West Coast with Eddie Heywood.
You were in California for a long time.
Well, for quite a while. I stayed there six or seven years, off and on. I went out there with Eddie

in...I think it was about '43 or something like that, or '44. And then we came back to New York and played the Three Deuces, I think. Then we went back again. Then came back again, and played Cafe Society Uptown. Then we went back again, and that's when I stayed out there. And I got sick out there, very sick. And I didn't come East until in '48, I think it was the Fall of '48... I came to Boston to play with Edmond Hall.
